thread.title: Four Arizona residents plead guilty in Pittsburgh drug trafficking case
thread.title_full: Four Arizona residents plead guilty in Pittsburgh drug trafficking case

author: Keystone Today
title: Four Arizona residents plead guilty in Pittsburgh drug trafficking case
text:
Troy Rivetti, U.S. Attorney's Office for the Western District of Pennsylvania | Department of Justice
Troy Rivetti, U.S. Attorney's Office for the Western District of Pennsylvania | Department of Justice
Four Arizona residents have pleaded guilty in federal court to charges connected to a large-scale drug trafficking and money laundering operation, according to Acting United States Attorney Troy Rivetti. The defendants were among 35 individuals indicted in January 2024 for their roles in an international narcotics and money laundering conspiracy involving fentanyl, methamphetamine, and cocaine.
The four individuals who entered guilty pleas before United States District Judge J. Nicholas Ranjan are Marcos Monarrez Jr., 26, of Phoenix; Erivan Guerrero, 25, of Phoenix; Donald Garwood, 43, of Glendale; and Jesus Aaron Garcia, 25, of Phoenix. Their plea hearings took place between July 30 and August 4.
According to information presented during the proceedings, from September to November 2022 Monarrez Jr., identified as a co-leader with his father of the Monarrez Drug Trafficking Organization based in Phoenix, was recorded via federal wiretap obtaining significant quantities of drugs from a Mexican supplier. These included hundreds of pounds of methamphetamine, millions of fentanyl pills, and kilograms of cocaine. The drugs were distributed by subordinate dealers across the country—including into western Pennsylvania—and more than $10,000 in proceeds was smuggled into Mexico to further support the operation.
Prosecutors said that all four defendants conspired with others to distribute substantial amounts of cocaine (five kilograms or more), fentanyl (400 grams or more), and methamphetamine (500 grams or more) within western Pennsylvania and other locations. They were also intercepted on federal wiretaps obtaining these substances for redistribution. From May 2022 through March 2023 Guerrero participated in money laundering by using bulk cash from drug sales for financial transactions designed to conceal its origins and promote the conspiracy. He also provided funds to suppliers knowing it would be sent to Mexico for the same purpose.
Monarrez Jr. additionally pleaded guilty to a separate charge out of Michigan for conspiring to distribute at least 400 grams of fentanyl between February 2019 and December 14, 2021.
Sentencing is scheduled for November 6, 2025 for Garcia, Guerrero, and Garwood; Monarrez Jr.’s sentencing is set for December 5, 2025. Monarrez Jr. faces mandatory life imprisonment under federal law while the other three could receive up to life sentences with fines reaching $10 million depending on factors such as offense severity and prior criminal history.
These latest pleas follow those already entered by twenty-two additional co-defendants—nine have been sentenced so far.
Assistant United States Attorneys Arnold P. Bernard Jr. and Tonya S. Goodman are prosecuting the case on behalf of the government.
The investigation was led by the Federal Bureau of Investigation’s Laurel Highlands Resident Agency along with Homeland Security Investigations https://www.justice.gov/hsi . Other agencies involved included Internal Revenue Service – Criminal Investigation https://www.irs.gov/compliance/criminal-investigation , United States Postal Inspection Service https://www.uspis.gov/ , as well as local law enforcement partners.
This prosecution falls under Operation Take Back America—a Department of Justice initiative focused on eliminating cartels and transnational criminal organizations through coordinated efforts like those conducted by Organized Crime Drug Enforcement Task Forces (OCDETFs) https://www.justice.gov/ocdetf/about-ocdetf-programs-0 and Project Safe Neighborhood (PSN) https://www.justice.gov/psn/about-project-safe-neighborhoods .
"Operation Take Back America streamlines efforts and resources from the Department’s Organized Crime Drug Enforcement Task Forces (OCDETFs) and Project Safe Neighborhood (PSN)."
